sections.intro: Worked bottom-up in the round: a stretchy ribbed brim, a cabled body, then crown decreases. The cable panel repeats every 6 rounds — the ×N marker keeps the count for you.
sections.outro: Cut yarn leaving a 20 cm tail, thread through remaining stitches, pull tight and weave in the ends on the inside. Block gently for the cables to bloom.

blocks.title: Brim
blocks.intro: Cast on 88 sts with a stretchy long-tail cast-on. Join in the round, being careful not to twist. Place a marker for the start of the round.

rows.text: K2, p2 to end of round.
rows.tip: Keep an even tension so the ribbing hugs the head.

blocks.title: Cable Body
blocks.intro: Set up the cable pattern across the round. Each 8-st panel is separated by p2 columns.
blocks.outro: Body measures about 15 cm from the cast-on edge.

rows.text: p2, k4, p2 — rep to end.
rows.note: This is the resting round between cable crosses.

rows.text: p2, k4, p2 — rep to end.
p2, C4F, p2 — rep to end.
rows.tip: Cross every cable the same way so the twist stays consistent.

rows.text: p2, k4, p2 — rep to end.

blocks.title: Crown
blocks.intro: Switch to DPNs when the stitches no longer fit around the circular. Decreases shape the top.

rows.text: p2tog, k4, p2tog — rep to end.
p1, C4F, p1 — rep to end.
p1, k2tog, k2tog — rep to end.

links.label: How to cross a cable without a cable needle

sections.content: For a slouchier fit, add one extra 6-round cable repeat before the crown. This beanie looks great in heathered naturals — cream, camel or forest green all show the cables beautifully. Care: hand wash cool, lay flat to dry.
